failures.description: self-attention, both add & normalize boxes, and feed-forward all use role 'neutral' and are visually identical apart from their text label. The reference distinguishes these by colour. Considered and rejected: none of the ten roles represents 'a computation step' as its own category separate from data (input/output/observed/prediction/etc.) - ROLE answers what an object MEANS, not which operation it performs - so 'neutral' for all four is the semantically correct choice, not a missed distinction. The boxes stay legible through their labels alone, which the case's own reference-notes.md treats as sufficient.

The two LayerNorm equations sit far to the right of their boxes with a large gap of empty space around them (particularly between 'feed forward' and its equation), lowering information density without adding clarity. Not a crossing or a correctness issue, just loose use of space.

reusableTechniqueFound: The residual connection needed a straight-line arrow to visually loop AROUND a box (self-attention, then feed-forward) rather than just point at it. Composed from two `line` segments (out and up, no arrowhead) plus one `arrow` segment (the final approach, with the head) - an L-shaped bypass. Two nested instances (bypass1 wraps self-attention at x=100, bypass2 wraps feed-forward at x=140, offset so they never visually merge) produced exactly the 'residual skips this one sublayer' picture with zero crossings. Naming this pattern (bypass-loop) alongside case02's spine-and-branch, for reuse in case09's encoder-decoder link.
